goal: Teach frontend-oriented AEM developers how versioned frontend source becomes browser-delivered clientlibs, how categories, dependencies and embeds form runtime contracts, and how to debug the artifact the browser actually received.

deck_context.source_summary: Class 12 of a seven-week AEM Sites course, delivered Tuesday, September 1, 2026. The audience understands AEM Resources, dialogs, persisted properties, HTL and browser evidence. This class connects the Week 3 Guide Card frontend source to the AEM clientlib build and delivery path.
deck_context.core_claim: A frontend change is complete only when versioned source is compiled into the intended clientlib category, included once by the correct owner and verified in the browser-delivered artifact.
canonical_facts: A client library is a cq:ClientLibraryFolder that organizes CSS, JavaScript and supporting resources.
The categories property provides logical runtime names used by pages and other clientlibs.
A clientlib below /apps uses allowProxy=true to be delivered through /etc.clientlibs.
css.txt and js.txt define ordered clientlib source entries.
WKND frontend source is edited below ui.frontend/src/main/webpack.
Webpack produces optimized output below ui.frontend/dist.
aem-clientlib-generator transforms distribution output into clientlibs below ui.apps.
Maven orchestrates the frontend build and deployable AEM package.
dependencies loads another category as a separate runtime contract.
embed combines selected library content into the current clientlib output.
The WKND archetype includes site and dependency categories through editable-template Page Policy.
Shared site assets should load once while Guide Card CSS and optional JavaScript remain narrowly scoped.
Browser debugging follows source import, build output, clientlib category, page inclusion, network response, cache and console evidence.

slides.title: Dependencies load; embeds combine.
slides.intent: Distinguish two clientlib graph operations and their browser-delivery effect.
key_points: dependencies loads required categories as separate contracts
embed combines selected library content into the current output
Use dependency when the other category remains independently delivered
Use embed when one owner intentionally assembles one delivery unit
Keep graphs small to avoid duplicates and hidden ordering

In the embed example, show one wknd.site output containing both contents. Do not claim that embed merely changes load order.

layout.intent: Make the delivery consequence visible instead of presenting property definitions as text only.

visual_elements.main_visual: Dependency graph versus embed graph with separate and combined browser artifacts.

constraints: Render the eyebrow exactly as '04 · DEPENDENCY GRAPH'.

slides.title: Load shared assets once; scope component assets narrowly.
slides.intent: Connect category inclusion to the narrowest owner of each frontend responsibility.
key_points: WKND site categories can be included through editable-template Page Policy
HTL helper can request CSS, JavaScript or both by category
Site shell, typography and tokens belong to the site bundle
Guide Card selectors begin at a project-owned component class
Avoid repeated global tags; add JavaScript only when native HTML and CSS are insufficient

local_context.required_background: Show one Page Policy including wknd.site once for a page that renders three Guide Card instances. Separate site-level shell, typography and tokens from .cmp-guide-card scoped CSS and optional instance-safe JavaScript. Contrast with a crossed-out repeated script/link injection per component instance.

layout.composition: One page-policy inclusion rail feeds a page with three Guide Cards; concentric ownership zones distinguish site bundle, scoped CSS and optional JavaScript.
layout.intent: Combine inclusion and scope because both answer who owns and loads the asset.

visual_elements.main_visual: Page Policy → one category request → three scoped Guide Card instances, with a crossed-out duplicate-inclusion pattern.

constraints: Render the eyebrow exactly as '05 · LOAD ONCE, SCOPE NARROWLY'.

Show one shared inclusion, not one request per component instance.
Do not make JavaScript mandatory for a static Guide Card.

slides.title: Debug the artifact the browser actually received.
slides.intent: Provide a repeatable diagnostic path for source that does not appear in the page.
key_points: Source file changed and is imported by the entry point
Compiled output and generated clientlib contain the change
Expected category is included by Page Policy or HTL
Page source and Network show the /etc.clientlibs/ request
Response content, cache and console explain the browser result
